title: An unramified ring map out of a field is étale
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra which is finitely generated as a $k$-algebra and whose module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{C/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is zero (that is, $k\to C$ is an unramified ring map, Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00UT). Then $k\to C$ is an étale ring map in the sense of Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00U1 as characterized in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]: $C$ is a finitely presented $k$-algebra, $H_1(L_{C/k})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\Omega_{C/k}=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00UW (algebra-lemma-unramified-at-prime, line 41568), lines 41584-41588: 'unramified over kappa(p) ... By Lemma 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field) it is smooth hence etale over kappa(p)'; the finite-presentation clause because k is Noetherian (Algebra, Lemma 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation)
